sub_skills.inclusion_test: The text (a) attributes a view/theory/assumption/expectation to someone ('some scholars claim', 'was thought', 'presumed', 'one theory', 'appeared to', 'often thought') or (b) marks two facts as in tension (however, but, nonetheless, even though, only partly, barring), AND the correct choice revises, limits, rejects, or reconciles that claim/tension (e.g., 'not conclusive', 'cannot say', 'did not depend on', 'contains later additions'). Apply only if INF.5 does not apply.

sub_skills.name: Generalize from specific cases
sub_skills.definition: Move from one or more specific instances in the text to a broader pattern, or name the general point a specific case illustrates.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The correct choice's subject is a broader class than the specific instance(s) the text describes (many organizations, a language, social media, the pricing model, scholarly regard for ephemera) or says the case 'illustrates/exemplifies' a general point. Apply only if INF.5 and INF.3 do not apply.

sub_skills.name: Infer a person's view or motive
sub_skills.definition: Infer what a named person or group believes, assumes, perceives, expects, wants, or would agree/disagree with, from what the text says they said, did, or hold.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The lead-in to the blank or the correct choice uses a mental-state frame from this closed list: in X's view; X thought/believed/assumed/perceived/anticipated/wanted; X would have disputed; X and Y likely agree; X may have determined; 'more important to X'; 'than X think'. The conclusion verbs conclude/suggest/hypothesize/posit/propose/reason/imply do NOT trigger it. Highest priority in tagging order.

sub_skills.name: Linking independent clauses
sub_skills.definition: Mark the boundary between two independent clauses with a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus a coordinating conjunction (and/but/so); avoid run-ons and comma splices.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when, in the correct answer, the blank sits between two independent clauses (each has its own subject + finite verb and could stand alone) and the correct mark is a period, a semicolon, or comma+FANBOYS. CB rationale typically says 'punctuation use between sentences' or 'coordination of main clauses'. A colon between two clauses goes to BND.4 instead. One tag per boundary: if the blank also contains a supplement boundary (e.g. ', though;'), add BND.2.

sub_skills.name: Setting off supplements and introductory elements
sub_skills.definition: Punctuate the edge of a nonessential (supplementary) element or an introductory/subordinate element: paired commas, dashes or parentheses around an interrupter, a comma after an introductory phrase or dependent clause, a comma before a trailing appositive/participial phrase or a supplementary adverb (however, though).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when a boundary in the blank is the opening or closing edge of an element CB calls 'supplementary', 'nonessential', 'aside', 'subordinate/dependent clause' or 'introductory phrase', and the correct mark there is a comma, dash or parenthesis (not a colon -> BND.4). Observable cue: the element can be deleted and the remaining sentence is still complete, or it is a dependent clause/phrase before or after a main clause.

sub_skills.name: No punctuation inside an integrated structure
sub_skills.definition: Recognize when nothing belongs at the blank because the words on either side form one grammatical unit: subject-verb, verb-object/complement, preposition-object, noun + essential modifier, title/label + name (restrictive appositive), integrated 'that' relative clause, or exactly two coordinated elements.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the correct answer has NO punctuation at the blank (and no conjunction is added) and CB's rationale says 'no punctuation is needed' / 'essential' / 'restrictive' / 'integrated'.

sub_skills.name: Colons and series punctuation
sub_skills.definition: Use a colon after a complete independent clause to introduce an explanation, elaboration, example or list; separate three or more series items with commas, or with semicolons when the items already contain commas (complex series).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the correct answer's mark at the blank is a colon, OR the blank sits between items of a series of three or more (simple or complex). Every series blank is BND.4 only, even if an item contains internal commas.

sub_skills.name: End-of-sentence punctuation (direct vs indirect question)
sub_skills.definition: Choose between a question mark and a period, and the matching word order, depending on whether the sentence asks a direct question or reports an indirect question / makes a statement.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the four choices differ in terminal mark (? vs .) and/or in question word order (auxiliary before subject vs subject before verb).

sub_skills.name: Subject-verb agreement
sub_skills.definition: Pick the verb form whose number (singular/plural) matches the head of the grammatical subject, including subjects that are relative pronouns, gerunds, 'each one of', titles, or compounds joined by 'and'.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Blank is (or contains) a finite verb AND either CB's rationale names 'subject-verb agreement' / says the verb 'agrees in number with the ... subject', or (if CB names no convention) the key is the only option whose verb number matches the subject while other finite options differ in number.

sub_skills.name: Verb tense and aspect
sub_skills.definition: Pick the tense/aspect (simple, progressive, perfect; past, present, future) that fits the passage's time frame, its other verbs, or its time markers.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: All options are finite verbs that agree with the subject in number (or number is not decisive) and differ in tense/aspect, AND CB's rationale justifies the key by tense ('express tense', 'consistent with the other ... tense verbs', past perfect, a time phrase).

sub_skills.name: Finite vs. nonfinite verb forms
sub_skills.definition: Decide whether the blank needs a conjugated (finite) verb to complete a clause, or a nonfinite form (to-infinitive, -ing participle, -ed participle, plain form after a modal) to build a modifying/supplementary phrase.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Options mix finite and nonfinite forms (to + verb, -ing, having + -ed, bare participle) AND the key is chosen because the clause does or does not already have a finite verb; CB's rationale says 'finite', 'nonfinite', 'infinitive', 'participle', or 'conjugated'.

sub_skills.name: Number and possession in nouns, pronouns, and determiners
sub_skills.definition: Choose the correct pronoun or determiner for its antecedent (it/they/them/this/these, its/their) and the correct plural vs. possessive spelling of nouns (apostrophe placement, its/it's, their/they're).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: What varies across the options is a noun, pronoun, or determiner (not a verb and not the clause's subject choice) - in number, in case/possession, or in apostrophe placement; CB's rationale names pronoun-antecedent agreement, possessive determiners, determiners, or plural/possessive nouns.

sub_skills.name: Subject-modifier placement
sub_skills.definition: Complete a sentence that opens with a modifying phrase so that the noun the modifier describes is the first noun phrase after the modifier's comma.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The sentence opens with a phrase ending in a comma before the blank, the options are full clauses beginning with different noun phrases, and CB's rationale names 'subject-modifier placement' or says the modifier and its subject must be next to each other.

clusters.display_name: account for a negation that reverses the meaning
clusters.definition: When not, hardly, no, less, unlikely, fail to, need not, by no means, declines to sits in front of the blank or claim, reverse the predicted meaning before choosing (and reverse twice for a double negative).

clusters.display_name: add and subtract the margin of error
clusters.definition: Form the plausible interval estimate - margin of error to estimate + margin of error.

clusters.display_name: add or subtract equations to eliminate a variable
clusters.definition: Add or subtract the two equations so one variable cancels.

clusters.display_name: add the parts to get the whole, or subtract to find a part
clusters.definition: Whole = sum of the parts: add pieces (lengths, areas, volumes, counts, cells) to get an unprinted total, or take the total minus the known parts to get a missing or leftover part (5 - x, t - 2).

clusters.display_name: apply an operation to every part of a compound inequality
clusters.definition: Multiply/add the lower and upper bounds of a range (a < x < b) to get the range of a derived quantity.

clusters.display_name: apply exponent rules
clusters.definition: Add exponents when multiplying like bases, subtract when dividing, multiply for a power of a power.

clusters.display_name: apply the quadratic formula
clusters.definition: Substitute a, b, c into x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2-4ac))/(2a) and simplify the radical.

clusters.display_name: cancel a common factor (noting the excluded value)
clusters.definition: Divide numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor, using the given domain restriction to justify it.

clusters.display_name: check a point in the equation or inequality
clusters.definition: Substitute an ordered pair (or each table row) and test whether the equation/inequality (each one in a system) is true.

clusters.display_name: check every part of the choice against the text
clusters.definition: Split a choice with two or three parts (or 'X because Y') and confirm each part against the text; one false part makes the whole choice wrong.

clusters.display_name: check that the second idea really follows from the first
clusters.definition: Test a cause/result option by asking whether the second idea is actually produced by or follows from the first (and not the reverse or merely next in time).

clusters.display_name: check that the subject can logically do the action
clusters.definition: Check that the subject of the word can actually do or be what the choice says (an inanimate delay cannot 'dispute'; a price rise cannot 'exploit').

clusters.display_name: check whether the specific case fits the general rule
clusters.definition: When one text states a general rule, problem or caution and another gives a particular case, check whether the case fits, breaks or solves the general statement.

clusters.display_name: check with a test value
clusters.definition: Substitute a convenient number (often 0 or 1) into the given expression and a choice to rule choices in or out.

clusters.display_name: classify the relationship between two views as agree, disagree, or qualify
clusters.definition: Decide whether one view fully agrees with, rejects, or partly accepts and limits the other before reading the choices.

clusters.display_name: clear fractions by multiplying by the common denominator
clusters.definition: Multiply both sides by the expression in the denominator (noting it cannot be zero).

clusters.display_name: combine like terms
clusters.definition: Add or subtract coefficients of terms with the same variable and the same exponent.

clusters.display_name: combine two facts to reach a conclusion
clusters.definition: Join two separately stated facts into the conclusion that follows from both together.

clusters.display_name: compare the values for the groups or conditions
clusters.definition: Compare the quantities in the notes (larger/smaller, highest, percentage vs. total) to see which choice states the comparison correctly.

clusters.display_name: complete the square
clusters.definition: Add and subtract (b/2)^2 to rewrite x^2+bx+c as (x+b/2)^2 plus a constant.

clusters.display_name: compute a frequency-weighted mean
clusters.definition: Sum value x frequency over all rows (or dot-plot columns) and divide by the total frequency.

clusters.display_name: compute a residual
clusters.definition: Find actual y minus the model's predicted y at the same x; its sign is decided by whether the point is above or below the model.

clusters.display_name: compute percent change from two values
clusters.definition: Compute (new - original) / original x 100 for a percent increase or decrease.

clusters.display_name: compute slope from two points
clusters.definition: Find (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) from two points, two table rows, or two graph points.

clusters.display_name: compute the discriminant
clusters.definition: Evaluate b^2-4ac and read its sign: positive two, zero one, negative no real solutions.

clusters.display_name: compute the mean
clusters.definition: Sum the values and divide by the number of values.

clusters.display_name: compute the range
clusters.definition: Subtract the minimum value from the maximum value.

clusters.display_name: convert between degrees and radians
clusters.definition: Multiply by pi/180 or 180/pi (or use 180 deg = pi).

clusters.display_name: convert between fraction, decimal, and percent
clusters.definition: Write p% of a quantity as (p/100) times the quantity, e.g., 60% of x as 0.6x, 7% tax as 1.07.

clusters.display_name: convert between radical and rational exponent
clusters.definition: Rewrite the n-th root of x^m as x^(m/n) and back.

clusters.display_name: convert diameter or circumference to radius
clusters.definition: Halve a diameter, or divide a circumference by 2pi, before using a radius-based formula.

clusters.display_name: convert units with a conversion factor
clusters.definition: Multiply by one or more unit fractions (e.g. 1 yard / 36 inches) arranged so unwanted units cancel; chained factors are the same action repeated.

clusters.display_name: distribute a negative sign
clusters.definition: When a parenthesized group is subtracted, change the sign of every term in it.

clusters.display_name: distribute over every term
clusters.definition: Multiply the outside factor by every term inside the parentheses.

clusters.display_name: divide polynomials
clusters.definition: Divide one polynomial by another (long division or rewriting the numerator in terms of the denominator) to get quotient plus remainder over divisor. Single EE instance.

clusters.display_name: eliminate choices that go beyond the text
clusters.definition: Cross out choices that bring in topics, comparisons, or claims the text (or neither text) mentions.

clusters.display_name: factor a trinomial
clusters.definition: Write ax^2+bx+c as a product of two binomials (find two numbers with the right sum and product).

clusters.display_name: factor by grouping
clusters.definition: Split the middle term, factor each pair, then pull out the shared binomial.

clusters.display_name: factor out the greatest common factor
clusters.definition: Pull the largest factor shared by every term (a number, a power of a variable, or a shared binomial) outside parentheses.

clusters.display_name: find a common denominator
clusters.definition: Rewrite fractions over one shared denominator before adding or subtracting them.

clusters.display_name: find a trig value on the unit circle
clusters.definition: Read cos/sin/tan from the coordinates of the unit-circle point, using the reference angle and the quadrant's signs.

clusters.display_name: find the sentence that answers the question
clusters.definition: Locate the sentence(s) that the question's named subject points to and answer from them, not from memory.

clusters.display_name: find the vertex with x = -b/(2a)
clusters.definition: Compute the axis of symmetry from standard form.

clusters.display_name: find what both sides accept beneath their disagreement
clusters.definition: When two texts disagree about a cause or meaning, find the fact or phenomenon both still take for granted.

clusters.display_name: generalize the listed examples into one idea
clusters.definition: When the text lists several details or examples, name the single quality or point they all share.

clusters.display_name: infer a feeling from a character's words and actions
clusters.definition: Work out a character's or speaker's feeling or attitude from what they do and say rather than from a stated label.

clusters.display_name: isolate the variable
clusters.definition: Undo operations in reverse order on both sides until the wanted variable stands alone.

clusters.display_name: join two complete sentences with a period, semicolon, or comma plus and/but/so
clusters.definition: Once both sides are complete sentences, pick a legal joiner and reject the comma splice and the run-on.

clusters.display_name: label what each sentence does
clusters.definition: Give each sentence a short role label (claim, example, prior view, method, finding, problem, solution, definition) and read the labels in order.

clusters.display_name: locate the median position in a frequency table
clusters.definition: Find the ((n+1)/2)th position, then accumulate frequencies (or plot dots/grouped rows) to find which value or interval holds it.

clusters.display_name: match a pronoun or determiner's number to the noun it refers to
clusters.definition: Choose singular (it, its, this) or plural (they, their, these, them) to agree with the antecedent.

clusters.display_name: match a verb to the parallel verb it pairs with
clusters.definition: When two verbs share a subject and are joined by and, put the blank in the same form and tense as its partner.

clusters.display_name: match coefficients
clusters.definition: Set coefficients of the same power equal on both sides of an identity.

clusters.display_name: match the data to the claim's groups and measure
clusters.definition: Check that an accurate data statement is about the same groups, measure and relationship the claim is about; reject accurate-but-irrelevant data.

clusters.display_name: match the function input to the given argument
clusters.definition: When f is defined on an expression such as f(3x), solve inner expression = given input first, then substitute.

clusters.display_name: match the positive or negative charge of the context
clusters.definition: Decide whether the context calls for a positive or negative word (or a mild versus harsh one) and drop choices with the wrong charge.

clusters.display_name: match the scope of the choice to the text
clusters.definition: Reject choices that cover only one detail when the question asks about the whole, or that widen the text's claim (all plants vs. one group).

clusters.display_name: match the strength of the claim
clusters.definition: Match how certain, strong, broad or hedged the answer is to what the text supports, using its qualifiers (some, may, only, all, not always; speculates vs proves).

clusters.display_name: match the verb's number to its subject
clusters.definition: Pick the singular or plural verb that agrees with the identified subject.

clusters.display_name: multiply a rate by the amount
clusters.definition: Total = rate x amount (distance = speed x time, cost = price x quantity, change in output = slope x change in input); divide to solve for the missing one.

clusters.display_name: multiply successive multipliers
clusters.definition: Chain two or more percent changes (or a percent of a percent) by multiplying their multipliers, not adding or subtracting the percents.

clusters.display_name: order the data and find the middle value
clusters.definition: Sort the list; take the middle value (odd n) or the average of the two middle values (even n).

clusters.display_name: pin down the exact claim in your own words
clusters.definition: Find the specific underlined or named claim (the 'conventional wisdom', 'what some researchers contend', a conclusion) and respond to that claim, not to the text in general.

clusters.display_name: predict the answer in your own words before reading the choices
clusters.definition: Before reading the choices, say what the blank or answer must mean, or how the two sentences relate (contrast, result, example, time), using the text's own clue.

clusters.display_name: punctuate a list: commas for three or more items, semicolons when items contain commas
clusters.definition: Separate items in a series with commas, upgrade to semicolons when any item has internal commas, and use no comma between just two coordinated items.

clusters.display_name: put a comma between an introductory or trailing phrase and the main clause
clusters.definition: Separate a leading subordinate clause or phrase, or a trailing participial or appositive phrase, from the main clause with a single comma.

clusters.display_name: put the noun the opening modifier describes right after it
clusters.definition: Identify who or what the introductory phrase describes and choose the version where that noun immediately follows the comma.

clusters.display_name: put the part over the whole
clusters.definition: Write the count or amount asked about over the count or amount of the whole reference group (a probability, a fraction, or x100 for 'what percent of').

clusters.display_name: rationalize the denominator
clusters.definition: Multiply by a conjugate (e.g., (2 - sqrt2)/(2 - sqrt2)) to clear a radical from a denominator.

clusters.display_name: read a box plot's five-number summary
clusters.definition: Read minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum from the whiskers and box lines of a box plot.

clusters.display_name: read a prediction off the model at a given x
clusters.definition: Go to the given x on the line/curve of best fit (not a data point) and read the model's y-value.

clusters.display_name: read a value from a table or graph
clusters.definition: Read the y-value at a given x (or an intercept, vertex, or maximum) off a graph.

clusters.display_name: read center and radius from standard form
clusters.definition: Read (h, k) with sign changes and r = sqrt(right side) from (x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2, or write the equation from a center and radius.

clusters.display_name: read the whole sentence after the blank before deciding
clusters.definition: Read to the end of the sentence containing the blank, because a later clause (a 'but', 'even in', 'yet') determines the relationship.

clusters.display_name: reduce a fraction or ratio to lowest terms
clusters.definition: Divide both parts of a fraction or ratio by their greatest common factor (7:28 -> 1:4, 12/48 -> 1/4).

clusters.display_name: reduce an angle by full rotations
clusters.definition: Subtract multiples of 2pi (360 deg) to get a coterminal angle between 0 and 2pi.

clusters.display_name: reject extraneous solutions
clusters.definition: Substitute candidate solutions back into the original equation and discard any that fail or make a denominator zero.

clusters.display_name: rescale the exponent for a different time unit
clusters.definition: Rewrite the exponent when the change happens every k units or the input unit changes (t/k, 12t months, q/4 quarters).

clusters.display_name: rewrite a negative exponent as a reciprocal
clusters.definition: Rewrite x^-n as 1/x^n (and 1/x^n as x^-n).

clusters.display_name: rewrite in slope-intercept form
clusters.definition: Solve a standard-form (Ax + By = C) or rearranged linear equation for y to expose slope and intercept.

clusters.display_name: round to the whole number the context allows
clusters.definition: After solving an inequality, take the greatest/least whole number that still satisfies it (round down for 'at most', up for 'at least').

clusters.display_name: rule out an alternative explanation
clusters.definition: Use a stated fact to eliminate a competing explanation, leaving the conclusion the text supports.

clusters.display_name: scale both quantities by the same factor
clusters.definition: When one quantity in a proportional relationship is multiplied by k, multiply the other by k (multiplicatively, not additively), without solving for individual values.

clusters.display_name: set a variable to zero to find an intercept or initial value
clusters.definition: Evaluate at x = 0 to get the y-intercept or starting amount.

clusters.display_name: set off removable information with a matching pair of commas, dashes, or parentheses
clusters.definition: Find the opening mark of an interruption already in the text (or supply both) and close it with the same mark.

clusters.display_name: set up and solve a proportion
clusters.definition: Write two equal ratios of corresponding quantities (similar-figure sides, arc to circumference, part angle to 360 deg or 2pi) and cross-multiply.

clusters.display_name: shift a graph by adjusting its equation
clusters.definition: Replace x with x-h to shift right h, add k to shift up k, and simplify.

clusters.display_name: simplify a radical
clusters.definition: Pull perfect-square factors out of a square root (sqrt(1,184) = 4sqrt(74)) or multiply radicals.

clusters.display_name: solve for the constant
clusters.definition: Solve the equation that the matched coefficients produce for the unknown constant.

clusters.display_name: split an absolute value equation into two cases
clusters.definition: From |A| = k (k >= 0), solve A = k and A = -k.

clusters.display_name: square both sides
clusters.definition: Isolate the radical, then square both sides to remove it.

clusters.display_name: square or cube a conversion factor for area or volume units
clusters.definition: Convert squared/cubed units (sq yd, m^3, s^2) by squaring or cubing the linear factor before applying it.

clusters.display_name: state what must be true for both facts to hold
clusters.definition: When two pieces of information are in tension, state the condition that lets both be true.

clusters.display_name: substitute a value and evaluate
clusters.definition: Substitute the input for x in the rule and simplify using order of operations.

clusters.display_name: substitute an expression
clusters.definition: Replace a variable or a group with the expression it is given to equal.

clusters.display_name: sum the face areas
clusters.definition: Find surface area by adding the areas of every face (pairs of congruent faces on a prism; 5 faces for an open box; overlap removed when solids are glued).

clusters.display_name: sum up the text's main point in one sentence
clusters.definition: State in one sentence what the whole text (or each text) is mainly saying before judging purpose or comparing texts.

clusters.display_name: take a percent of a quantity
clusters.definition: Compute p% of a whole as (p/100) x whole.

clusters.display_name: take the square root of both sides
clusters.definition: From (expression)^2 = k (or ^3), take the root of both sides: keep both + and - for an equation; keep only the positive root when the quantity is a length.

clusters.display_name: tell a possessive pronoun from a contraction (its/it's, their/they're)
clusters.definition: Use its or their for possession and it's or they're only where "it is" or "they are" fits.

clusters.display_name: test each answer choice
clusters.definition: Plug each choice into the condition and keep the one that satisfies it.

clusters.display_name: translate a circle by moving its center
clusters.definition: Shift a circle by adding the shift to its center's coordinates (radius unchanged), then rewrite its equation.

clusters.display_name: translate figurative language into plain meaning
clusters.definition: Turn a metaphor, simile, or personification into a plain statement of what it shows about a character, feeling, or scene.

clusters.display_name: translate words into an equation or inequality
clusters.definition: Name the unknown and write the relationship described in words as an equation or function.

clusters.display_name: treat a ratio as side lengths with a common multiplier
clusters.definition: Turn a given trig ratio such as cos A = 3/5 into sides 3n and 5n, find the third side, then scale to the given length.

clusters.display_name: turn a percent change into a multiplier
clusters.definition: Turn 'p% longer/increased' into multiplication by (1 + p/100) before substituting.

clusters.display_name: undo a percent change by dividing by the multiplier
clusters.definition: Recover the original value from a changed value by dividing by (1 +/- p/100).

clusters.display_name: use a colon only after a complete sentence to introduce an explanation, example, or list
clusters.definition: Place a colon only where the words before it form a complete sentence and the words after it explain, specify, or list.

clusters.display_name: use an apostrophe only to show possession, placed for a singular or plural owner
clusters.definition: Ask "does something belong to it?" and "is there more than one?"; add 's for one owner, s' for plural owners, and no apostrophe for a plain plural.

clusters.display_name: use dates or time words to set the order of events
clusters.definition: Line up dates and time words (already, in 1928, as decades passed) to decide whether the new event is earlier, later, repeated, or final.

clusters.display_name: use interval endpoints to bound a statistic
clusters.definition: With grouped data (histogram bins, table ranges, tanks), use each interval's least/greatest possible value to bound a mean or to place the median.

clusters.display_name: use supplementary angles
clusters.definition: Use that angles forming a straight line (linear pair, angles on a line) sum to 180 deg.

clusters.display_name: use the distance formula
clusters.definition: Compute the length between two coordinate points with sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2).

clusters.display_name: use the exterior angle theorem
clusters.definition: Set an exterior angle of a triangle equal to the sum of the two remote interior angles.

clusters.display_name: use the midpoint formula
clusters.definition: Use that a center/midpoint is the average of the endpoint coordinates (or that equal distances locate the center) to find a missing point.

clusters.display_name: use the negative-reciprocal slope for a perpendicular line
clusters.definition: The slope of a perpendicular line is -1/m (horizontal vs vertical when m is 0 or undefined).

clusters.display_name: use the past perfect (had + verb) for the earlier of two past events
clusters.definition: When one past action finishes before another past action, put the earlier one in had + past participle.

clusters.display_name: use the Pythagorean theorem
clusters.definition: Write a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with the hypotenuse as c and solve for the missing side.

clusters.display_name: use the reference-sheet formula
clusters.definition: Substitute the given dimensions into the standard area, perimeter, circumference, or volume formula and evaluate.

clusters.display_name: use the sum and product of the solutions
clusters.definition: For ax^2+bx+c=0 use sum = -b/a and product = c/a (or build the equation from its roots) without finding each root.

clusters.display_name: use the triangle angle sum
clusters.definition: Use that the interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 deg (the two acute angles of a right triangle sum to 90 deg).

clusters.display_name: use the zero product property
clusters.definition: Set each factor of a product equal to zero and solve each.

clusters.display_name: use total = mean x count
clusters.definition: Convert a mean into a sum (sum = mean x n) to find a missing/removed value, a combined mean, or an unknown in a list.

clusters.display_name: work backward from a part to the whole
clusters.definition: Given a part and the percent it represents, solve (p/100) x whole = part for the whole.

clusters.display_name: work out what result the claim predicts
clusters.definition: Ask 'if this claim were true, what would we observe?' and pick the evidence that shows that (or its opposite, for weaken).

clusters.display_name: write a trig ratio as opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse
clusters.definition: Read sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj for a named acute angle, or use one to find a side.

clusters.display_name: write an exponential model a(1 +/- r)^t
clusters.definition: Use the initial amount as a and 1 + r (growth) or 1 - r (decay) as the base.

clusters.display_name: write y = mx + b from slope and a point
clusters.definition: Put the slope in for m, then use the y-intercept or substitute a known point to find b.

clusters.display_name: check whether each side of the punctuation is a complete sentence
clusters.definition: Test the words before and after the blank for a subject and a finite verb (and no subordinator) to decide whether it is a clause seam.

clusters.display_name: check whether the clause still needs its main verb
clusters.definition: Decide whether the clause already has a finite verb: if not, the blank must be conjugated; if so, the blank is a to-verb or -ing/past-participle phrase.

clusters.display_name: check whether the sample was random
clusters.definition: Ask whether the sample was randomly drawn from the whole target population; a convenience, self-selected, or one-subgroup sample is biased, whatever its size.

clusters.display_name: classify growth as linear or exponential
clusters.definition: Constant amount of change per unit -> linear; constant percent/factor of change per unit -> exponential; direction gives increasing vs decreasing.

clusters.display_name: compare coefficients and constants to count solutions
clusters.definition: Equal x-coefficients (proportional coefficients for a system) with unequal constants give no solution; fully equivalent sides/equations give infinitely many; otherwise exactly one.

clusters.display_name: compare spread visually
clusters.definition: Judge standard deviation from how many values sit far from vs. close to the center (shape of histogram/dot plot, or a reported SD).

clusters.display_name: decide whether the added information is essential or removable
clusters.definition: Delete the phrase and reread: if the sentence still identifies the same thing and stays grammatical, the phrase is removable (punctuate it); if not, it is essential (no punctuation).

clusters.display_name: decompose a figure into simpler shapes
clusters.definition: See that a figure splits into (or is boxed by) triangles/rectangles whose measures are easy, e.g., a square cut by its diagonals, a triangle enclosed in a rectangle, an extra segment drawn to create a triangle.

clusters.display_name: describe the trend of a scatterplot
clusters.definition: Identify whether the data increase or decrease and whether the trend is straight or curved.

clusters.display_name: distinguish 'p% of' from 'p% more/less than'
clusters.definition: Recognize that 'p% of x' is (p/100)x while 'p% greater than x' is (1 + p/100)x and 'p% less than x' is (1 - p/100)x.

clusters.display_name: distinguish a data value from its frequency
clusters.definition: In a frequency table/bar graph/dot plot, keep apart the value (horizontal axis or 'Value' column) and how many times it occurs (bar height or 'Frequency').

clusters.display_name: find the cause-and-effect signal word
clusters.definition: Spot because, since, so, thus, therefore, consequently, due to, as a result (including the connector right before the blank) and use it to know whether a cause, effect or conclusion is needed.

clusters.display_name: find the claim the new sentence actually connects to
clusters.definition: Identify which earlier sentence or clause the new one responds to; it may be the second sentence, a clause after a semicolon, or a claim rather than the most recent fact.

clusters.display_name: find the clue that restates the blank
clusters.definition: Locate the phrase (often after a colon, dash, 'that is', or in the next sentence) that says the same thing as the blank in other words.

clusters.display_name: find the contrast signal word
clusters.definition: Spot a word or phrase such as but, however, although, unlike, instead, rather, on the other hand, despite, whereas that tells you the two parts point in opposite directions.

clusters.display_name: find the true subject by skipping the interrupting phrase
clusters.definition: Bracket off modifiers or interrupting phrases to find the head noun of the subject (and where it ends), including inverted or delayed subjects.

clusters.display_name: follow a comparison word to the term being compared
clusters.definition: Use comparatively, less, more, as ... as to find the other thing being compared and make the answer its opposite or match.

clusters.display_name: identify the base quantity (the 'of' or 'per' denominator)
clusters.definition: Decide which quantity is the whole/original/'per' unit a percent or rate refers to (original vs new value, row total vs grand total, land area vs total area).

clusters.display_name: identify the hypotenuse
clusters.definition: Take the side opposite the right angle (equivalently the longest side) as the hypotenuse, and so locate the right angle.

clusters.display_name: identify the transversal angle pair
clusters.definition: Name the pair formed by a transversal across parallel lines (corresponding / alternate interior equal; same-side interior or exterior supplementary); every angle is one of only two measures, acute or obtuse.

clusters.display_name: identify which clause a transition word belongs to
clusters.definition: Decide from the logic of the passage whether a conjunctive adverb (however, though, rather, for example) ends the first clause or opens the second, and put the semicolon or period on the correct side of it.

clusters.display_name: interpret a function statement f(a) = b
clusters.definition: Read f(a) = b as "at input a, the output is b", in the units of the context.

clusters.display_name: judge what the audience already knows
clusters.definition: Decide whether the audience needs a term or background explained (unfamiliar) or would find it redundant (already familiar), and keep or cut it accordingly.

clusters.display_name: keep subject, verb, object, and preposition together with no punctuation
clusters.definition: Recognize that the blank splits two core sentence parts that are never separated by punctuation.

clusters.display_name: locate the matching cell or total in a table
clusters.definition: Find the row/column (or total) whose labels match the wording of the question.

clusters.display_name: match a number in the model to its meaning in context
clusters.definition: Match a constant, coefficient, base, intercept or vertex of a model to what it means (initial value, rate, time, maximum) in the context's units.

clusters.display_name: match corresponding parts from the vertex order
clusters.definition: Use the stated correspondence (A to D, B to E...) to pair angles and sides of congruent/similar figures.

clusters.display_name: match equation parameters to graph features
clusters.definition: Use the sign/size of slope and y-intercept (or the sign of the leading coefficient and the intercept/vertex of a quadratic, or b < 1 vs b > 1 for an exponential) to pick the model equation that fits the graph.

clusters.display_name: match the conclusion to the population sampled
clusters.definition: Generalize only to the group the random sample was drawn from - not a larger group, not just the sample itself, not a subset of it.

clusters.display_name: merge categories that together meet the condition
clusters.definition: Notice that the condition (e.g. 'at least 10', 'neither blue nor yellow') covers several rows/columns/categories and combine them.

clusters.display_name: pick the equivalent form that displays a value
clusters.definition: Choose the rewritten form whose coefficient, constant, or base equals the asked value (f(0), f(1), maximum, y-intercept).

clusters.display_name: read slope and intercept from the equation
clusters.definition: In y = mx + b (or f(x) = b + mx) see m as the slope/rate and b as the y-intercept without computation.

clusters.display_name: read the title, axes, key, and scale before the data
clusters.definition: Notice that an axis does not start at 0, has non-unit gridlines, or is labeled in a shifted unit (years since 1940, days after Jan 11) before reading values or slope.

clusters.display_name: read the vertex from vertex form
clusters.definition: From a(x-h)^2+k, the vertex is (h, k) and k is the max (a<0) or min (a>0).

clusters.display_name: read the zeros from factored form
clusters.definition: From a(x-p)(x-q)..., the zeros are p, q, ... (repeated factors count once as x-intercepts).

clusters.display_name: recognize a difference of squares
clusters.definition: See that a^2 - b^2 (including radicals or squared groups) factors as (a-b)(a+b).

clusters.display_name: recognize a perfect-square trinomial
clusters.definition: See that a^2 + 2ab + b^2 is (a+b)^2.

clusters.display_name: recognize a proportional relationship
clusters.definition: A line through the origin (or a table with constant ratio y/x) means y = kx with b = 0.

clusters.display_name: recognize a special right triangle
clusters.definition: Identify a 45-45-90 (legs x, hypotenuse x sqrt2) or 30-60-90 (x, x sqrt3, 2x) triangle from its angles, equal legs, a tangent of sqrt3, or an equilateral triangle's altitude.

clusters.display_name: recognize a square cannot equal a negative
clusters.definition: See that a squared quantity is never negative, so (expression)^2 = negative has no real solution.

clusters.display_name: recognize all radii are equal
clusters.definition: Use that segments from the center to points on a circle are radii and so have the same length.

clusters.display_name: recognize an isosceles triangle
clusters.definition: Use equal sides (stated, or two radii) to conclude equal base angles, or equal angles to conclude equal sides.

clusters.display_name: recognize equal angles have equal trig ratios
clusters.definition: Use that corresponding angles of similar right triangles (or equal angles anywhere) have the same sine, cosine and tangent.

clusters.display_name: recognize parallel lines have equal slopes
clusters.definition: A parallel line shares the slope; only the intercept may change.

clusters.display_name: recognize similar triangles
clusters.definition: Find two pairs of equal angles (shared angle, right angles, vertical angles, parallel-line angles) to conclude triangles are similar (AA), including nested and 'bow-tie' figures and the altitude to a hypotenuse.

clusters.display_name: recognize sin of an angle equals cos of its complement
clusters.definition: Use sin x = cos(90 deg - x): the two acute angles of a right triangle, or two angles with sin of one equal to cos of the other, are complementary.

clusters.display_name: recognize that a constant shift preserves spread
clusters.definition: Adding the same number to every value shifts center measures by that number but leaves range and standard deviation unchanged.

clusters.display_name: recognize the shaded side of a boundary line
clusters.definition: Match a shaded half-plane to the inequality direction (above: y > ..., below: y < ...), with solid vs dashed boundary.

clusters.display_name: recognize the solution as the intersection point
clusters.definition: Read the coordinates (or count) where two given graphs cross.

clusters.display_name: recognize the two acute-angle tangents are reciprocals
clusters.definition: Use tan of one acute angle = 1 / tan of the other acute angle in a right triangle.

clusters.display_name: recognize vertical angles
clusters.definition: See that angles opposite each other at an intersection are equal.

clusters.display_name: recognize when evidence can't settle the question
clusters.definition: Notice that the evidence leaves a question open (alternative reading, undated, no clear evidence) so the right conclusion is a limit, not a verdict.

clusters.display_name: restrict to the given condition's row or column
clusters.definition: Notice a 'given that' / 'of the ...' / 'if the one chosen is ...' condition and use that subgroup's total, not the grand total, as the denominator.

clusters.display_name: scale lengths by k, areas by k^2, volumes by k^3
clusters.definition: Recognize that when every length is multiplied by k (similar figures or a stated dimension change), perimeter scales by k, area by k^2 and volume by k^3; or run it backward (area ratio -> k by square root).

clusters.display_name: see that extreme values pull the mean, not the median
clusters.definition: An extreme value or a long tail on one side pulls the mean (and range/SD) toward it but leaves the median unchanged or barely changed.

clusters.display_name: see the right triangle inside the figure
clusters.definition: Notice a right triangle hidden in another figure: rectangle diagonal, cone radius/height/slant height, radius and tangent, two radii with a right central angle, equilateral triangle altitude, inscribed polygon.

clusters.display_name: set aside information the question doesn't need
clusters.definition: Notice that a table or number in the stem is not needed for what is asked and ignore it.

clusters.display_name: spot a concession before the main claim
clusters.definition: Notice when a text grants a point (acknowledging, while, although, certainly, nevertheless) before making its real claim, and separate what is granted from what is argued.

clusters.display_name: spot a word used in an uncommon sense
clusters.definition: Notice that a familiar word is used in a less common meaning here and reject choices that give its everyday meaning.

clusters.display_name: spot comparison wording (both, whereas, while, unlike)
clusters.definition: Recognize whether a choice's wording expresses similarity ('both', 'like', 'also') or difference ('whereas', 'while', 'unlike', 'even though') and match it to what the goal asks.

clusters.display_name: spot that the target expression can be reached without solving
clusters.definition: Notice the asked-for expression (3x + 8, x - 7, 39x, x + y, 2x - 1) is a multiple, shift, or sum of what the given equation(s) already contain.

clusters.display_name: spot the turn from a common view to the real point
clusters.definition: Notice a text that gives a common/long-held view or background and then turns (often with but, however, yet) to the point the author or new finding makes; the old view is not the answer.

clusters.display_name: take an unusual transition at its literal meaning
clusters.definition: When the keyed-looking word is not a standard logic connector (fittingly, there, increasingly, again and again, in many cases), read its literal meaning and check it against the content.

clusters.display_name: tell a direct question from a reported question
clusters.definition: Check whether the sentence asks the question itself (inverted order plus question mark) or reports it inside a statement (subject-verb order plus period).

clusters.display_name: tell a general claim from a specific example
clusters.definition: Distinguish a broad statement about a category from a specific instance, so a 'generalization', 'definition' or 'explanation and example' goal gets the right level (or both levels).

clusters.display_name: tell a population mean apart from individual values
clusters.definition: Recognize that an interval for a mean says nothing about where every (or most) individual value lies.

clusters.display_name: tell an example from a restatement or a specification
clusters.definition: Distinguish an instance of a broader claim (for example) from the same idea in other words (in other words, that is) and from more precise detail of the same thing (specifically, to be exact).

clusters.display_name: tell describing from arguing
clusters.definition: Decide whether the author is informing/describing or arguing/recommending, and reject purpose verbs (argue, criticize, urge) the text does not do.

clusters.display_name: tell evidence from interpretation
clusters.definition: Separate what was observed or measured from what someone concluded from it, and from models or assumptions, so you can see what a critic is targeting.

clusters.display_name: tell growth from decay by the base
clusters.definition: A base above 1 means growth, between 0 and 1 means decay; a decreasing exponential has no minimum on an open domain.

clusters.display_name: trace a pronoun or 'this' back to what it refers to
clusters.definition: Find the noun or earlier idea a pronoun, determiner or pointing word (it, they, this, such, these) stands for, even with other nouns in between.

clusters.display_name: track whose view each sentence presents
clusters.definition: Keep straight who holds each view (the author, a named researcher, critics, 'some scholars', a common assumption) so an answer does not credit a view to the wrong person.

clusters.display_name: translate 'at least / at most' into an inequality symbol
clusters.definition: Map at least / minimum to >=, at most / no more than / maximum to <=, between to a compound inequality.

clusters.display_name: treat a random sample's rate as the population's rate
clusters.definition: Recognize that a random (representative) sample's proportion or mean is the best estimate for the population, so it can be scaled up.

clusters.display_name: treat a repeated expression as one unit
clusters.definition: Notice a repeated group (x^2-x, x-7, x^2) and treat it as a single variable.

clusters.display_name: treat a sample statistic as an estimate, not an exact value
clusters.definition: Reject statements that the population value (or another sample's value) is exactly, or certainly, the sample value; keep 'best estimate' / 'plausible'.

clusters.display_name: treat an arc as a fraction of the circle
clusters.definition: See arc length / circumference = central angle / 360 deg (or / 2pi); arcs together make the full circle; arc measure equals central angle.

clusters.display_name: turn the goal into a checklist of required parts
clusters.definition: Split the goal into every part it demands (both items, 'study and its findings', 'duration and purpose', 'generalization and support', 'explanation and example', a quotation) and require all of them in the answer.

clusters.display_name: use symmetry to locate the mean
clusters.definition: In a symmetric distribution the mean equals the median, at the center of symmetry.

clusters.display_name: use tangent facts
clusters.definition: Use that a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency (slopes are negative reciprocals; tangent to an axis means r = distance from center to that axis) and that two tangent segments from one outside point are equal.

clusters.display_name: use the complement
clusters.definition: Find the share not in a category as 100% minus the given percent(s).

clusters.display_name: use the symmetry of a parabola
clusters.definition: The vertex x-value is the average of two inputs with equal outputs (e.g. the two zeros).

clusters.display_name: use time clues in the text to choose the verb tense
clusters.definition: Locate the date, sequence, or surrounding verb that fixes when the action happens, and choose the tense that fits that time frame.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph a circle and read its center and radius
clusters.definition: Type the circle equation in any form; click the top and bottom points and use midpoint(...) for the center and distance(...)/2 for the radius.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: convert a decimal result to a fraction
clusters.definition: Answer-form utility for any Math skill: convert a decimal Desmos result to a fraction with the fraction button; never answers a question alone.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: rename the variable to x before graphing
clusters.definition: Utility move: rename the equation's letter (t, n, p, w) to x before graphing; it never answers a question alone.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph and compare equivalent forms
clusters.definition: Graph the original and each choice; the equivalent one overlaps exactly (toggle it to see the overlap).

clusters.display_name: Desmos: define f(x) and evaluate it
clusters.definition: Define f(x) = ..., then evaluate f(3) or a combination; a table of inputs, or the same test input in the expression and each choice, is the same move.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph an inequality and test the shaded region
clusters.definition: Graph the inequality or system; a point is a solution if it is inside the shaded region (the overlap for a system), not on a dashed edge.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: fit a model through points by regression
clusters.definition: Enter the points in a table and fit y_1 ~ m x_1 + b (or a quadratic or exponential) to read the parameters (r^2 = 1 for an exact fit).

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph and click the vertex (max or min)
clusters.definition: Graph y = the expression and click the vertex (x or y as asked); on a restricted domain also evaluate the endpoints.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph each side and read the crossing x
clusters.definition: Type the equation as written (a vertical line) or each side as y = ..., and read the x of the line or crossing, never its y.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: test choices as parameterized points on a slider
clusters.definition: Enter each choice as a point in a parameter (r) with a slider; the right one stays on the line as r moves.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: compute a percent or multiplier as typed arithmetic
clusters.definition: Type a percent, a multiplier (1 + 27/100) or a percent change ((92 - 45)/45*100) and read the value; the same typed-arithmetic move covers a chained unit-conversion computation.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: test whether a point lies on a graph
clusters.definition: Type the point and see whether it sits on the graphed circle or line.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: compute list statistics (mean, median)
clusters.definition: Type mean(...), median(...) of the data; for a missing value, graph mean or median of a list containing x.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph a system and click the intersection
clusters.definition: Graph both equations and click the crossing for (x, y); parallel lines mean no solution, the same line infinitely many.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: define a translated function and read its feature
clusters.definition: Define f, then g(x) = f(x + h) + k, hide f, and read the feature of g asked for.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: evaluate a trig value in degree mode
clusters.definition: Type sin(56) (or cos, tan) after switching the settings to degrees for a degree question; read the value.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: solve for an unknown constant with a slider
clusters.definition: Put the unknown constant on a slider (widen its bounds) or type each choice's value, until the condition holds.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: find exact constants by regression
clusters.definition: Regression between two expressions, [left] ~ [right] with subscripted variables and conditions, to read exact constants.

clusters.display_name: Desmos: graph and click the zeros
clusters.definition: Graph y = the expression (or left side minus right side) and click the gray points on the x-axis.

clusters.display_name: Direct Factor Application
clusters.definition: Problems solved by a single multiplication or division using a given conversion factor or rate. The student identifies whether to multiply or divide and applies the factor once.

clusters.display_name: Cross-Multiplication
clusters.definition: Problems solved by setting up two equivalent ratios as a proportion (a/b = c/d), cross-multiplying, and solving the resulting linear equation for the unknown. Includes finding missing table entries via constant-ratio reasoning.

clusters.display_name: Ratio-to-Expression Translation
clusters.definition: Problems solved by interpreting a stated ratio and translating it into an algebraic expression involving a variable. The student must understand that scaling both parts of a ratio by the same factor preserves the ratio.

clusters.display_name: Conversion-Factor Chaining
clusters.definition: Problems solved by multiplying or dividing by two or more conversion factors in sequence, including squaring or cubing a linear factor for area/volume unit conversions.

clusters.display_name: Density Formula Application
clusters.definition: Problems solved by applying the density formula (density = total / area-or-volume), rearranging to solve for the unknown quantity, and in some cases first computing volume from a side length using V = s^3.

clusters.display_name: Multi-Operation Rate-Proportion Composition
clusters.definition: Problems requiring a primary rate or proportion step followed by one or more additional arithmetic operations: percentage calculation, subtraction of two derived quantities, algebraic substitution, scale-factor geometry, or currency conversion with surcharge.

clusters.display_name: Proportion Setup and Solve
clusters.definition: The student sets up the proportion part/whole = rate/100 (or its equivalent: part = rate/100 * whole) and solves for the single unknown by one multiplication or one division. This is the foundational solving pattern for PCT.1, PCT.2, and PCT.3.

clusters.display_name: Percent-Change Formula Application
clusters.definition: The student identifies old and new values, computes their difference, divides by the old value, and multiplies by 100. May include a preliminary step of reading values from data. This is the solving pattern for PCT.5.

clusters.display_name: Single-Multiplier Construction or Interpretation
clusters.definition: The student converts a verbal percent relationship into a single decimal multiplier ((1+r/100) or (1-r/100)) and either applies it to compute a value (PCT.4), writes it as an expression (PCT.7), or reads it from a given expression (PCT.8). The key step is recognizing the equivalence between 'p% more than x' and '(1 + p/100) * x'.

clusters.display_name: Multiplier Chaining
clusters.definition: The student constructs and composes two or more multipliers in sequence: multiply the quantity by the first multiplier, then by the second. For markup-then-discount: final = original * (1 + markup/100) * (1 - discount/100). The key insight is that the second percent acts on the intermediate result, not the original.

clusters.display_name: Reverse Division (Undo a Percent)
clusters.definition: The student divides a known result by the multiplier that produced it to recover the original value. For example, if the final price after a 20% discount is $80, divide by 0.80 to get the original $100. The key step is recognizing that undoing a percent requires division, not subtraction.

clusters.display_name: Transitive Substitution Across Percent Links
clusters.definition: The student expresses each quantity in terms of another using a = (p/100)*b notation, substitutes one equation into another to eliminate the intermediate variable, and simplifies to find the target percent. For example: a = 2.30b and a = 0.60c yields c = 2.30b/0.60 = 3.833b, so c is approximately 383% of b.

clusters.display_name: Data Extraction Then Percent Computation
clusters.definition: The student reads one or more numerical values from a table, bar chart, or line graph, then performs a percent calculation (find part, find percent, or percent change) on the extracted values. The data-reading step precedes and is prerequisite to the percent step.

clusters.display_name: Nested Subset Computation
clusters.definition: The student applies a first percent to a total to get a subtotal, then applies a second percent to that subtotal (not to the original total). Alternatively, the student uses complementary percents (100% minus the sum of stated percents) to find a remainder category, then works with that remainder. The key step is recognizing which quantity each percent applies to.

clusters.display_name: Direct Ratio from Counts
clusters.definition: Compute the probability of an event by counting the favorable outcomes and dividing by the total number of equally likely outcomes. The favorable and total counts are given directly or can be read from a single description.

clusters.display_name: Probability via Complement or Multi-Step Counting
clusters.definition: Compute a probability that requires either complement reasoning (P = 1 - P(not event)) or combining counts from multiple groups before forming the ratio. The favorable count is not directly stated but must be derived.

clusters.display_name: Restricted Sample Space Ratio
clusters.definition: Compute a conditional probability by restricting the sample space to a given condition, then finding the ratio of favorable outcomes within that restricted space. Often involves reading a row, column, or subset from a table.

clusters.display_name: Count Recovery from Probability
clusters.definition: Reverse the probability formula: given P(event) and the total (or the count and P), solve for the missing count. May require complement reasoning or subtracting known counts first.

clusters.display_name: Complement and Multi-Step Counting
clusters.definition: Compute a count or probability by using complement reasoning (total minus known) or by combining multiple probability statements to recover a missing count before forming the final ratio.

clusters.display_name: Algebraic Probability Equation
clusters.definition: Set up and solve an algebraic equation where the unknown is a count or a total, given one or more probability values. The probability formula P = favorable/total is rearranged to isolate the unknown.

clusters.display_name: Read One-Way Table and Compute Ratio
clusters.definition: Read a single-variable frequency table, locate the target category count, compute the total by summing if not provided, and divide.

clusters.display_name: Read Two-Way Table Marginals
clusters.definition: Locate the appropriate row or column total in a two-way table, read the grand total, and compute the marginal probability.

clusters.display_name: Read Two-Way Table Cell for Joint Probability
clusters.definition: Locate the intersection cell representing two simultaneous conditions in a two-way table, read the grand total, and divide.

clusters.display_name: Graph/Table Value Extraction
clusters.definition: Locate and read numerical values (bar heights, dot counts, box-plot features, table cells) from a data display. The core step is visual-to-numeric translation.

clusters.display_name: Sum-and-Divide (Mean Computation)
clusters.definition: Add all data values (or compute frequency-weighted sums) and divide by the total count to produce the arithmetic mean. This is the procedural core of any question that asks for a mean.

clusters.display_name: Order-and-Locate (Median Finding)
clusters.definition: Sort data values (or use cumulative frequencies) and identify the middle position(s) to determine the median. For n values, locate position (n+1)/2 (odd) or average positions n/2 and n/2+1 (even).

clusters.display_name: Max-Minus-Min (Range Computation)
clusters.definition: Identify the greatest and least data values and subtract to find the range. May involve reading extremes from a display first.

clusters.display_name: Algebraic Mean Inversion
clusters.definition: Set up the mean equation (sum / count = known mean), substitute known values, and solve algebraically for the unknown quantity. Includes forward (find x given mean) and reverse (find removed value given old and new mean) variants.

clusters.display_name: Weighted-Average Combination
clusters.definition: Combine two or more group means into an overall mean using the weighted-average formula: total sum = n1*mean1 + n2*mean2; combined mean = total sum / (n1 + n2).

clusters.display_name: Distribution-Shape Reasoning
clusters.definition: Use visual or conceptual properties of a distribution's shape (symmetry, skewness, concentration near the mean, outlier presence) to infer relationships between statistics. Includes comparing SDs by eyeballing spread, determining mean vs. median order from skew, and recognizing that shifting does not change SD.

clusters.display_name: Data-Modification Effect Analysis
clusters.definition: Reason about how a specific change to a data set (adding/removing a value, adding a constant to all values, replacing a value) propagates to each summary statistic. Requires understanding which stats are affected by the specific type of change.

clusters.display_name: Statistic Identification and Selection
clusters.definition: Given a described property or a set of answer choices, identify which statistical measure (mean, median, mode, range, SD) matches the description, or determine which measure can or cannot be computed from the given information.

clusters.display_name: Direct Graph Reading
clusters.definition: Locate a value on one axis, trace horizontally or vertically to the graph/data point, and read the corresponding value on the other axis.

clusters.display_name: Slope Computation (Rise over Run)
clusters.definition: Select two points (on a line or from data), compute (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1), and express the result as a decimal or fraction.

clusters.display_name: Sign and Intercept Reasoning
clusters.definition: Determine the sign of the slope (positive or negative) and the approximate y-intercept from a graph to eliminate answer choices or classify the relationship.

clusters.display_name: Pattern Recognition in Data (Differences vs. Ratios)
clusters.definition: Examine successive differences or successive ratios in a table, or the curvature of a graph, to distinguish linear growth (constant differences) from exponential growth (constant ratios) or quadratic behavior.

clusters.display_name: Residual and Deviation Analysis
clusters.definition: Compute actual value minus predicted value for a specific data point, using the model line/curve to find the predicted value.

clusters.display_name: Contextual Slope and Rate Interpretation
clusters.definition: Translate the numerical slope into a per-unit statement (e.g., 'for each additional unit of x, y increases by m') and connect the y-intercept to the starting value in context.

clusters.display_name: Substitution and Evaluation
clusters.definition: Plug a given x-value into a model equation and evaluate to find the predicted y, or test candidate equations by substituting known data points.

clusters.display_name: Interval rate-of-change computation
clusters.definition: Computing (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) across one or more intervals from a graph or table to find average rate of change, or comparing rates across intervals to identify the steepest segment.

clusters.display_name: Nonlinear model fitting by key features
clusters.definition: Matching a scatterplot's curved pattern to a specific quadratic or exponential equation by testing key features such as vertex, y-intercept, direction of opening, or exponential base.

clusters.display_name: Compute sample statistic from raw data
clusters.definition: Calculate a sample proportion or sample mean from counts or individual values provided in the question stem, before using it for inference.

clusters.display_name: Construct confidence interval from estimate and MOE
clusters.definition: Apply the formula estimate +/- margin of error to determine the interval of plausible values for the population parameter.

clusters.display_name: Scale sample proportion to population count
clusters.definition: Multiply the sample proportion (or its complement) by the total population size to estimate the number of individuals in the population with a given characteristic.

clusters.display_name: Distinguish population parameter from individual values
clusters.definition: Recognize that the margin of error describes uncertainty about the population mean or proportion, NOT the range of individual values in the population or sample.

clusters.display_name: Evaluate whether a specific value is plausible
clusters.definition: Determine whether a particular value falls inside or outside the confidence interval, using language like 'plausible', 'doubtful', or 'not possible' appropriately.

clusters.display_name: Relate sample size to margin of error
clusters.definition: Understand that a smaller sample size generally produces a larger margin of error, and vice versa, because smaller samples are less representative.

clusters.display_name: Identify correct population for generalization
clusters.definition: Determine which population a sample statistic can be generalized to, based on how the sample was selected (e.g., largemouth bass vs all fish; adults who own TVs vs all adults).

clusters.display_name: Identify the sampled population
clusters.definition: Determine the specific group from which the sample was actually drawn, distinguishing it from broader or narrower groups mentioned in the question.

clusters.display_name: Detect non-representative sampling
clusters.definition: Recognize that a sample drawn from a convenience location, voluntary response, or non-random subgroup is not representative of the target population and will produce biased estimates.

clusters.display_name: Recognize inherent uncertainty in sampling
clusters.definition: Understand that even a valid random sample gives an estimate, not an exact value, and that repeating the sampling process can yield different results.

clusters.display_name: Resist over-generalization
clusters.definition: Reject conclusions that extend beyond the population from which the sample was selected -- e.g., from one school to all schools, from dog owners to all residents, or from book-likers to all moviegoers.
